f3_program: collection("john.doors_to_replace", "door", "john", source("3 bedroom doors and two outside doors to replace"))
observe(at("john.doors_to_replace.bedroom.count", "current"), 3, "count", source("3 bedroom doors"))
observe(at("john.doors_to_replace.outside.count", "current"), 2, "count", source("two outside doors"))
observe(at("john.doors_to_replace.outside.replacement_cost_per_door", "current"), 20, "dollar_per_door", source("outside doors cost $20 each to replace"))
fraction_of("john.doors_to_replace.bedroom.replacement_cost_per_door", "john.doors_to_replace.outside.replacement_cost_per_door", 1, 2, source("the bedroom doors are half that cost"))
query("value", "john.doors_to_replace.total_replacement_cost")
assumptions: The phrase "that cost" refers to the per-door replacement cost of an outside door.
The total payment covers replacing every bedroom and outside door stated.
The intended averaging set appears to be the two displayed years, 2018 and 2019.
F3-v1 cannot express a difference between two separately computed means as one terminal query without introducing query-derived mean relations.
The requested total basic-earnings-per-share figures appear on table rows whose row-label cells are empty.
F3-v1 requires a non-empty exact row label for cell evidence, so those totals cannot be grounded canonically.

f3_program: collection("angela.kitchen_supplies", "kitchen_supply", "angela", source("Angela's kitchen supplies"))
observe(at("angela.kitchen_supplies.pots.count", "current"), 20, "count", source("20 pots"))
offset("angela.kitchen_supplies.plates.count", scale("angela.kitchen_supplies.pots.count", 3), 6, "count", source("6 more than three times as many plates as the pots"))
fraction_of("angela.kitchen_supplies.cutlery.count", "angela.kitchen_supplies.plates.count", 1, 2, source("half as many cutlery as the plates"))
collection("sharon.kitchen_supplies_to_buy", "kitchen_supply", "sharon", source("kitchen supplies Sharon wants to buy"))
fraction_of("sharon.kitchen_supplies_to_buy.pots.count", "angela.kitchen_supplies.pots.count", 1, 2, source("half as many pots as Angela"))
offset("sharon.kitchen_supplies_to_buy.plates.count", scale("angela.kitchen_supplies.plates.count", 3), -20, "count", source("20 less than three times as many plates as Angela"))
multiple("sharon.kitchen_supplies_to_buy.cutlery.count", "angela.kitchen_supplies.cutlery.count", 2, source("twice as much cutlery as Angela"))
query("sum", "sharon.kitchen_supplies_to_buy", "planned")
assumptions: Amounts of cutlery are treated as counts of individual kitchen-supply items, as implied by the requested total number.

f3_program: collection("party.attendees", "person", "party", source("people attended the party"))
collection("party.attendees.women", "woman", "party", source("60 women at the party"))
observe(at("party.attendees.women.count", "current"), 60, "count", source("60 women at the party"))
fraction_of("party.attendees.women.married.count", "party.attendees.women.count", 3, 4, source("three-fourths of these women were married"))
collection("party.attendees.men", "man", "party", source("men at the party"))
collection("party.attendees.husbands", "husband", "party", source("their husbands with them to the party"))

add("married_women_brought_husbands", "party.attendees.women.married", at("party.attendees.count", "current"), "party.attendees.husbands.count", source("brought their husbands with them to the party"))
fraction_of("party.attendees.men.single.count", "party.attendees.men.count", 3, 4, source("3/4 of the men at the party were single"))
query("value", "party.attendees.count")
assumptions: The source does not state that the husbands brought by the married women exhaust all non-single men at the party.
Without that population-closure assertion, the total number of men and therefore attendees is not uniquely constrained.
